Merch 29, 1927
Mr'. Ches. A. Inaberen, Inc.,
c/o Fyen Airlines,
San
Diego, California.
Dear Mr. Iindbergh:
I have just received your letter of the 26th with further
reference to the rebuilt Wright Whirlwind.
Seotty mas "all lit up" about the prospecte of getting a
wielwind but I think from your description that he has been saved
You are quite right when you say that the performance
of this motor is a remaricable tribute to the fright Company, and
at least gives a good idea of the service that one can expect
from a real Thirlwind.
Last night I spent some time with Manford Mellider, who
came through St. Louis with Capt. G. R. Irwin.
I was talling to
Ervin about new developments in comerelal seaplanes, and he told
me that there were a number of types being manufactured on the
mest cost.
I have an idea, which
may some day materialize, wherein
we will need a flykig boat for use on the Mississippi. Preferably,
it should have a metallle mull, deaigned so ae to resist ordinary
driftwood. "lthout going to any special trouble, 1f you could get
some information along this 11ne for me, I would be very grateful.
The ship I may want will be a job for the water somewhat similar
to my Travel-Air, but I do not believe the Travel-Air would be made
entirely practical for river worle by the addition of pontoons.
Am delighted to mow that your monoplane is progressing
rapidly and that you plan to be ready to take off on the date
named. That date, of course, we must contine to leep secret.
with lindest regards,
and again thanking you for all
that you have done in my behalf, I am
yury sincerely,
